text: THE DE-ADDICTION LOCATOR NO LONGER LISTS FOUR CENTRES TWICE, AND NO LONGER RISKS DROPPING ONE. Two separate defects, found from a React duplicate-key error in the console. (1) The national feed returns 487 rows carrying 483 centres: four ODIC records repeat with every field identical — name, type, address, district, state and point. A record with nothing to tell it from another is not a second centre, so `unpack` drops the copies where `normaliseGeo` already runs, and no caller can forget it. The published count moves 487 → 483 with it, because a typed 487 above a list of 483 is two answers to one question (`data-state-completeness.md` §2); the type counts now sum to the total exactly, and the classic map reads "478 centres plotted, of 483 geo-tagged". (2) Eight more pairs share a name and a point while differing in type or address — "Sankalp Sanskritik Samiti" in Raipur is an IRCA on a building's ground floor and an SLCA on its first — and the locator keyed a centre on its name, point and district alone. Two map pins carried one id, which React may answer by dropping one of them, so a citizen could have been shown one of the two centres at an address and not the other. The key carries the type and the address now. Nothing that differs between two records is merged: the comparison is every field, not a chosen few.
